title: Upgrade to support OpenMRS Platform 3.0
body:
Updates reportingrest so it builds against, and runs on, openmrs-core master (Platform 3.0.0-SNAPSHOT: Java 21, Jakarta EE, Spring 7). It depends on the reporting upgrade (openmrs/openmrs-module-reporting, platform 3.0 PR). Same approach as the platform 3 upgrades of calculation (openmrs/openmrs-module-calculation#19), legacyui and webservices.rest.

## Changes
- Versions and build:
  - Module version is now 3.0.0-SNAPSHOT. It builds against core 3.0.0-SNAPSHOT (with `openmrs-bom` imported), webservices.rest 5.0.0-SNAPSHOT, reporting 3.0.0-SNAPSHOT, htmlwidgets 3.0.0-SNAPSHOT, serialization.xstream 1.0.0-SNAPSHOT and calculation 3.0.0-SNAPSHOT.
  - Builds with Java 21 and `-parameters`, with surefire 3.5.3.
  - `javax.servlet-api`, the javax/powermock exclusions and `hamcrest-all` are removed.
- `config.xml` now sets `require_version` to 3.0.0.
- Jackson 1 becomes Jackson 2 in the ad hoc model and resources. REST 5 serializes with Jackson 2, so the `@JsonProperty` annotations now take effect.
- commons-lang becomes lang3, and javax.servlet/persistence become jakarta.
- Tests:
  - Migrated to JUnit 5.
  - `EvaluatedResourceTest` now uses Spring's `MockHttpServletRequest`.
  - `AdHocQueryResourceTest.testRowFilterQuery` expects `{7}` for the "encounter during period" filter. Core's test dataset moved patient 2's only encounter out of that window (TRUNK-6569), and the combined result is unchanged.
- CI (Bamboo, release workflow) uses JDK 21.

## Verification
- `mvn clean install` passes (59 tests).
- On openmrs-core master with openmrs/openmrs-core#6631 and #6633 (`mvn jetty:run`, MySQL 8), in the full set of 26 upgraded O3 modules:
  - All modules start, and logging in through the UI works.
  - `reportingrest/reportDefinition`, `cohortDefinition` and `dataSetDefinition` return 200.
  - `POST reportingrest/adhocquery` evaluates a patient data set with a built-in cohort row filter and returns the expected rows.
- reporting itself needs #6633 to start on core master.

title: (docs) Replace the dead Travis badge with the GitHub Actions one
body:
The README badge still points at travis-ci.org, which shut down and now redirects to a 404, so the badge renders blank. This module builds on GitHub Actions via build.yml, so this points the badge and its link there.

Heads up that the badge will show red right now: the latest build.yml run on master failed on 2026-09-03. In this repo it's the Java 17 build job as well as the OWASP dependency check.

title: REPORT-922 - Support endpoint that can immediate run and render report
Separate OWASP dependency check into its own job
body:
## Summary
- Separate OWASP dependency check into a standalone workflow job
- OWASP check only runs on push and workflow_dispatch (not on PRs)
- Build job no longer runs the OWASP check inline or needs the NVD_API_KEY secret

## Test plan
- [ ] Verify build job still passes
- [ ] Verify OWASP dependency check runs on push to the default branch
- [ ] Verify OWASP dependency check does not run on pull requests

title: O3-5519: Add BOT_GH_TOKEN to build workflow secrets
body:
- Ticket Link - [https://openmrs.atlassian.net/browse/O3-5519](url)
- Ticket ID - O3-5519

## Summary

The shared OWASP Dependency Check workflow (`openmrs-contrib-gha-workflows`) has been updated to automatically push generated vulnerability reports to the central dashboard repository ([openmrs-contrib-dependency-vulnerability-dashboard](https://github.com/openmrs/openmrs-contrib-dependency-vulnerability-dashboard)).

To support this, the reusable workflow now requires the `GH_BOT_TOKEN` secret to be passed by calling repositories. Without it, the workflow cannot push reports to the dashboard.

## Change

Added `BOT_GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.OMRS_BOT_GH_TOKEN }}` to the `secrets` block in `.github/workflows/build.yml`.
